text: prove that sin(x)/x approaches 1 as x approaches 0, and explain it

Given: Angles are measured in radians., 0<x<\frac{\pi}{2} for the unit-circle comparison., The inscribed triangle lies inside the sector, and the sector lies inside the outer tangent triangle., \sin(-x)=-\sin x., \cos x is continuous at x=0.
Find: \displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sin x}{x}

1. State the limit and restrict the domain
   lim ₓ→ ₀(sin x)/(x)=1
   We will prove the limit first for small positive angles, specifically 0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}. Angles are measured in radians, which is essential because the sector area is then \frac{x}{2}.

2. Construct the unit-circle comparison
   Area of inscribed triangle=(1)/(2)sin x, area of sector=(x)/(2), area of outer triangle=(1)/(2)tan x
   Consider a unit circle centered at O. Let A=(1,0), and let B be the point on the circle reached by rotating through an angle x, where 0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}. Draw the chord AB, the tangent to the circle at A, and the radii OA and OB. The triangle OAB lies inside the sector AOB, and the sector lies inside the triangle formed using the tangent at A.

3. Compare the three areas
   (1)/(2)sin xle (x)/(2)le (1)/(2)tan x
   Because the inscribed triangle is contained in the sector, its area is no greater than the sector area. Because the sector is contained in the outer tangent triangle, its area is no greater than the outer triangle area. The inequalities may be strict for 0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}, but non-strict inequalities are sufficient for the squeeze argument.

4. Obtain the fundamental trigonometric inequality
   sin xle xle tan x
   Multiply every part of the area inequality by 2. Since 2 is positive, the inequality directions do not change. Thus the geometric comparison becomes \sin x\le x\le\tan x.

5. Divide by the positive angle
   (sin x)/(x)le 1le (tan x)/(x)
   For 0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}, we have x>0. Therefore, dividing each part of \sin x\le x\le\tan x by x preserves the inequality directions.

6. Rewrite the upper comparison using tan x
   (tan x)/(x)=(sin x)/(xcos x)
   Use the identity \tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}. Substituting this into the right-hand side gives \frac{\tan x}{x}=\frac{\sin x}{x\cos x}.

7. Derive the lower bound for sin(x)/x
   1le (sin x)/(xcos x) Longrightarrow cos xle (sin x)/(x)
   Since x>0 and \cos x>0 for 0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}, we may multiply the inequality 1\le\frac{\sin x}{x\cos x} by the positive quantity \cos x. This yields \cos x\le\frac{\sin x}{x}. Combining this with the earlier upper bound gives the desired squeeze:

8. Establish the squeeze inequality
   cos xle (sin x)/(x)le 1 (0<x<(π)/(2) )
   The left inequality comes from the tangent comparison, and the right inequality came directly from \sin x\le x. Thus, for every sufficiently small positive x, the quotient is trapped between \cos x and 1.

9. Evaluate the two bounding limits
   lim ₓ→ ₀^₊cos x=cos 0=1, lim ₓ→ ₀^₊1=1
   The cosine function is continuous at 0, so its limit as x approaches 0 from the right equals its value at 0. The constant function 1 has limit 1.

10. Apply the squeeze theorem from the right
   1=lim ₓ→ ₀^₊cos xle lim ₓ→ ₀^₊(sin x)/(x)le lim ₓ→ ₀^₊1=1
   Since the lower and upper bounds have the same right-hand limit, the squeeze theorem forces the middle function to have that same limit.

11. Use evenness to obtain the left-hand limit
   (sin (-x))/(-x)=(sin x)/(x)
   Because sine is odd, \sin(-x)=-\sin x. Therefore the quotient \frac{\sin x}{x} is an even function. Its values for negative x match its values at positive x, so the left-hand limit equals the right-hand limit.

12. Conclude the two-sided limit
   boxed lim ₓ→ ₀(sin x)/(x)=1
   The right-hand limit equals 1 by the squeeze theorem, and the left-hand limit is equal to it because \frac{\sin x}{x} is even. Therefore the two-sided limit is 1.

Answer: boxed lim ₓ→ ₀(sin x)/(x)=1
For 0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}, unit-circle geometry gives \sin x\le x\le\tan x. Dividing by x>0 and rewriting \tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} gives \cos x\le\frac{\sin x}{x}\le 1. As x\to0^+, both bounds approach 1, so the squeeze theorem gives \lim_{x\to0^+}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1. Since \frac{\sin(-x)}{-x}=\frac{\sin x}{x}, the function is even, so the left-hand limit is the same. Hence \displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1.

operations.title: The limit we will prove
operations.caption: \lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1
operations.narration: We want to understand why sine of a very small angle is almost the same as the angle itself. We will first prove the result for positive angles between zero and pi over two, measured in radians.

operations.title: Three regions in the circle
operations.caption: \text{Area of inscribed triangle}=\frac{1}{2}\sin x,\qquad \text{area of sector}=\frac{x}{2},\qquad \text{area of outer triangle}=\frac{1}{2}\tan x
operations.narration: Take a unit circle centered at O. Let A be the point at one o'clock on the horizontal axis, and let B be reached by rotating through angle x. The chord triangle is inside the sector, and the sector is inside the triangle made with the tangent at A.

operations.title: Compare the areas
operations.caption: \frac{1}{2}\sin x\le \frac{x}{2}\le \frac{1}{2}\tan x
operations.narration: The inscribed triangle cannot be larger than the sector containing it. The sector cannot be larger than the outer tangent triangle containing it. Therefore their areas are ordered from left to right.

operations.title: From areas to lengths
operations.caption: \sin x\le x\le\tan x
operations.narration: Multiply every part by two. Because two is positive, the inequality directions stay the same. The geometric area comparison becomes an inequality involving sine, the angle, and tangent.

operations.title: Divide by the angle
operations.caption: \frac{\sin x}{x}\le 1\le\frac{\tan x}{x}
operations.narration: Since x is positive in our chosen interval, dividing by x does not reverse either inequality. This gives an upper bound of one and a lower comparison involving tangent.

operations.title: Rewrite the tangent bound
operations.caption: \frac{\tan x}{x}=\frac{\sin x}{x\cos x}
operations.narration: Use the identity tangent x equals sine x divided by cosine x. The right-hand comparison now contains the quotient we are trying to study, together with a cosine factor.

operations.title: Reveal the lower bound
operations.caption: 1\le\frac{\sin x}{x\cos x}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\cos x\le\frac{\sin x}{x}
operations.narration: For an angle between zero and pi over two, cosine is positive. So we may multiply by cosine without reversing the inequality. This produces the lower bound we need.

operations.title: The squeeze is visible
operations.caption: \cos x\le\frac{\sin x}{x}\le 1\qquad\left(0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}\right)
operations.narration: We now have both sides. For every sufficiently small positive x, the quotient sine x over x is trapped between cosine x and one.

operations.title: Both bounds approach one
operations.caption: \lim_{x\to 0^+}\cos x=\cos 0=1,\qquad \lim_{x\to 0^+}1=1
operations.narration: As x approaches zero from the right, cosine approaches its value at zero, which is one. The constant upper bound is already one. Both boundaries therefore approach the same number.

operations.title: Squeeze from the right
operations.caption: 1=\lim_{x\to 0^+}\cos x\le\lim_{x\to 0^+}\frac{\sin x}{x}\le\lim_{x\to 0^+}1=1
operations.narration: The quotient remains between two functions whose right-hand limits are both one. The squeeze theorem forces the middle quotient to approach one as well.

operations.title: Crossing to negative angles
operations.caption: \frac{\sin(-x)}{-x}=\frac{\sin x}{x}
operations.narration: To handle negative x, use the fact that sine is odd. The two minus signs cancel in the quotient, so the function has the same value at x and at negative x. Its left and right behavior at zero must therefore agree.

operations.title: FINAL ANSWER
operations.caption: \boxed{\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1}
operations.narration: The squeeze theorem gives the right-hand limit as one, and evenness gives the same value from the left. Therefore, as x approaches zero from either side, sine x divided by x approaches one.
